findings.description: Test adequacy: no test fails if `COMMAND=${COMMAND//\\n/$nl}` is deleted.
findings.body:
**Test adequacy: nothing pins the `\n` decode in the no-jq branch.**

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/45c01595b830832d8e07a518f0c5403d0177c266/.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh#L26-L26

```bash
COMMAND=${COMMAND//\\n/$nl}
```

No payload in `tests/hooks/git-safety.test.sh` contains a JSON `\n`. The force-push and `reset --hard` rules are substring matches, and the escaped-tab case (L40-41) only exercises the `\t` line. So deleting this line leaves the whole suite green.

This line matters. It is the only thing that lets an end-anchored rule see a line break inside a multi-line command. Without it, `{"tool_input":{"command":"git push origin main\nls"}}` leaves `git push origin main\nls` with a literal backslash after `main`. The trunk rule needs `main` to be followed by a blank, the end of the line, or `[|&;]`, so it doesn't match and the hook exits 0. With jq, the same payload is blocked, because `jq -r` decodes the newline and `grep` matches line by line. The validator traced both paths and confirmed this.

`docs/conventions/testing.md` §Principles: "A bug fix lands with a regression test that fails without the fix."

**Fix:** add a case to `tests/hooks/git-safety.test.sh` after L45:

```bash
expect 2 'without jq, an escaped newline ends the line a rule anchors on' "$T/bin" \
  '{"tool_input":{"command":"git push origin main\nls"}}'
```

findings.description: Every no-jq payload puts `tool_input` first, so the `${nl}command$nl:` strip never runs on the real Claude Code shape (session_id, cwd, tool_name… before tool_input). Changes to the prefix handling, such as swapping `#*` for `##*`, would go unnoticed. Add a case such as `'{"session_id":"a\"b","cwd":"C:\\x","tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"git push origin main"}}'` expecting 2.

The bare-push case only checks that `git push` on the trunk blocks. Nothing checks that a bare `git push` on a feature branch passes, so a change that blocked every bare push would leave the suite green. Add the same subshell case in a repo created with `git init -q -b feature/x`, expecting exit 0.

No no-jq payload contains an escaped backslash (`\\`), so deleting the mark-and-restore steps (L20 and L28) passes the suite. No exit-code difference was found under today's rules, so this is an unpinned edge, not a defect. A case like `"command":"echo C:\\\\"` expecting 0 would pin it, and so would a payload with no `command` key.

The new comment says "with every escaped pair set aside", but only `\\` and `\"` are set aside (`\n` and `\t` are decoded afterwards), and it doesn't say that an escaped quote becomes `'`. Suggested wording: "with escaped backslashes and quotes set aside (an escaped quote becomes `'`)".

The push-to-trunk rule doesn't catch a quoted refspec such as `git push origin "main"`. With jq the `"` remains, and without jq it becomes `'`, and neither fits the rule's optional `src:` / `refs/heads/` prefix. The gap comes from the regex, not this delta.

process_issues.description: The quality reviewer did not read `docs/conventions/core.md` or the `ci-and-agent-config` skill checklist, so its convention checks used only the injected `testing.md`. Coverage of core.md's comment and Altitude clauses on this 31-line delta relies on its own judgment, not quoted text.
